steps: Locate the fireplace

Plan the unit, vent and gas line together: a peninsula wall, an island or between two interior walls, out of traffic and away from furniture and draperies. Install to local codes or, without them, CSA B149.1 (Canada) or ANSI Z223.1/NFPA 54 (USA).

• "Front" = the side with access to the electrical connection compartment cover and the gas valve connection; facing it, the control compartment cover and the coaxial vent on top are to your left.
  • Qualified (licensed or trained) installers only. Massachusetts: only a licensed Plumber and Gas Fitter may install it, and for side wall horizontally vented equipment terminating less than seven (7) feet above grade, 248 CMR 5.08 requires carbon monoxide detectors and a vent sign (p. 4).
  • Manufactured (mobile) homes: in some jurisdictions after the "first sale"; consult local codes. The fireplace must be fastened in place (CAN/CSA Z240 MH; Title 24 CFR, Part 3280 or ANSI/NFPA 501A).
  • Suitable for a bedroom or bed sitting room. Never connect it to a chimney flue serving a separate solid fuel burning appliance.
  • Door frame removal (p. 6): unit off and cool; remove the safety barrier screen and any trim kit; release the two spring-loaded latches with the one-piece latch handle, holding the glass; tilt the frame top out and lift it off its bottom track. The ceramic glass is very fragile.
Framing kit: assemble & attach

Assemble the two identical steel stud frames, one for each side, with the side without screw holes facing out. With the fireplace in its final position, secure each frame to the unit's framing brackets, bend the tabs out 90 degrees and fasten them to the wood framing.

1. Kit TCWS.54STFRKIT, joined with #8 x 1/2 wafer screws; stand the parts on their narrow ends. Lay out the two upper/lower studs (74 5/8" L) as top and bottom; screw three center studs (25" L) below the top one, the inner cross brace across their lower ends, then a side stud (54 1/16" L) at each end.
  2. Lower cross brace, screen tab slots up, about 12" from the lower ends of the side studs; then the lower horizontal stud and the two outer side studs. Turn the frame over and screw the other face.
  3. Align with the framing brackets and secure with two framing bracket screws through the access holes in the outer side studs. The assembled frames act as the top and side standoffs.

The fireplace should be in place and the venting installed before framing in. Nothing combustible inside the steel stud framing: no combustible material, electrical wiring, insulation, plastic vapor barrier or gas plumbing. A full header above the framing kit is highly recommended; other framing can be conventional lumber. Seal the chase at the ceiling or between floors. Insulate outer chase walls to the same degree as other exterior walls and cover the insulation and vapour barrier with a solid surface such as drywall; don't place the fireplace directly against insulation, and don't insulate or use plastic vapour barrier inside the framing kit.
Set the front: fixed lintel

The lintel is fixed, so move the fireplace itself to set the front, using the framing kit's 1 7/8" adjustment along the framing brackets. Allow for the facing thickness, and swap the lintel edge (flanged or hemmed) if needed.

Allow for the facing thickness (1/2 inch calcium silicate board or a rock facing) before settling on the final position of the fireplace.

Lintel edge

The lintel ships with the flanged edge out; it can be turned to the hemmed edge.

  1. Remove the safety barrier screen and the decorative door trim.
  2. Loosen the securing bolts in the upper and lower corners on each side and remove the lintel. Move the two safety screen magnets to the opposite side of the lintel.
  3. Rotate it so the desired edge faces away from the fireplace, remount it and tighten the bolts.
  4. Refit the door trim and the safety barrier screen.
Board, facing & hearth

Sheet the front with non-combustible backer board 12" above and 5 9/16" to the side of the framing edge bars (drywall screws). Finish flush (facing up to 1 7/8" thick) or recessed, and keep 6" min. between the bottom of the glass door and a combustible hearth.

• Backer board (not supplied): cement board or its equivalent; standard drywall beyond the 12" / 5 9/16" zone. Calcium silicate board is 1/2" thick and can be damaged if dropped or struck: inspect it, don't use it if cracked, and pre-drill the mounting holes.
  • If the board won't be finished with other non-combustible material such as tile, single sheets of calcium silicate board are recommended for the top sections; taped and mudded joints may crack from the heat.
  • Painting the wall above? Discard the framing kit and frame with full sheets of calcium silicate board and full length metal studs.
  • Flush: facing up to 1 7/8 of an inch thick (p. 15); p. 8 notes that 3/4" facing finishes flush with the front of the unit. Minimum combustible framing dimensions are a drawing only (Figure 13, p. 9).
  • Hearth extension not required, and combustible flooring may run up to the base, but wood flooring and the like may discolor, shrink or crack from the radiant heat. Any object higher than 11 9/16" will interfere with the door frame opening.
  • Facing must never stop the door or the screen from opening: the glass door must be able to open if excess gas buildup ignites.
Note: the manual gives two recess depths. It says the unit may be recessed up to 6" with noncombustible masonry type material (p. 5) and that masonry type non-combustible material can go up to 6 inches forward of the appliance (p. 8), but gives a 4 1/2 inch recess on p. 15 and a 4 1/2 maximum facing depth in Figure 12 (p. 9).
Electrical, wall switch & remote

Check the NV / PV switch on the IFC board is set to PV, connect the wall switch cable, wire 110 V. AC to the junction box and mount the wall switch with no batteries. Install the burner, leak-check, then test: wall control to ON sparks the igniter, then the pilot and main burner light.

1. Control box: bottom left-hand side, below the firebox floor. Reach in and push the switch away from you to PV (Power Vent); this model must be pre-set to PV.
  2. Connect the wall switch / home automation cable to the connector just forward of the power vent switch.
  3. Connect 110 V. AC to the wires in the junction box: black power in, two white neutrals, blue to the power vent (its wiring is also accessed here).
  4. Attach the wall switch to the framing and route the 40 ft cable. Leave its battery holder empty.
  5. Install the burner per the burner kit instructions, turn on the gas and check every connection is tight and leak free.
  6. Turn on gas and electrical supplies and move the center button on the wall control to "ON": the igniter sparks, and after a short delay the pilot lights, followed by the main burner.

Remote & home automation

Link the remote: selector to REMOTE, press the internal PROGRAM button once with a straightened paper clip, wait for 3 beeps, press ON/OFF on the remote; 3 more beeps and it's programmed. Keep the toggle on REMOTE to use the remote. (The Owner's Manual, p. 11, first links the wall switch to the fireplace.) Home automation: a dry contact relay switches flame and light on/off; a 0 - 10 volt DC signal modulates them (Low = 1 volt, High = 10 volts). The control repeats a signal every 2 hours or until a new command.
Gas supply & leak test

Run the gas line through the access holes beneath the fireplace on the flue side of the control box to the 3/8" N.P.T. valve inlet. Fit a drip leg in the supply line and a union or flanged connection just upstream of the valve, then leak-test every connection.

• Gas line by a qualified service person to all building codes, with the correct line diameter for proper operation and pressure.
  • Drip leg in the supply line to the gas control valve, to keep scale and dirt out of the valve. (Warranty condition: sediment traps within 6 feet of the gas control valve.)
  • The union or flanged connection goes inside the control compartment so the valve can be repaired or replaced.
  • Service is from inside the unit through the access panel in the firebox bottom. Reinstall the access panel and its gasket afterwards, or the control system will overheat and fail early.
  • Pressure testing the piping: disconnect the appliance and its shut-off valve above 1/2 psig (3.5 kPa); close its manual shut-off valve at or below 1/2 psig.
Power vent & vent run

This fireplace must be power vented: wall terminate with the TCVT.PV1.25 or TCVT.PV7.110 kit, roof terminate with TCVT.PVCV. Join, screw and tape every outer joint, and support the pipe at least every 4'.

• Follow the instructions supplied with the power vent kit; this kit is for the TCWS54.DST only. Electrical work by a qualified electrician (CSA C22.1 / ANSI/NFPA 70); never use a rheostat on the supply.
  • Vent speed by run length: TCVT.PV1.25 LOW at 0 - 6', HIGH at 7'- 25'; TCVT.PV7.110 LOW at 7'- 25', HIGH at 26'-110'.
  • 110 ft maximum plus six 90-degree elbows, 66 foot maximum vertical rise; 3 ft minimum plus one 90-degree elbow. Any mix of rise and run, including up to 3 ft below the unit (to the center of the vent pipe).
  • Minimum vent length chart (TCWS54DST, p. 24): A, minimum rise from floor to flue center 49" / 61" / 73"; B, pipe length 0" / 12" / 24"; C, min. pipe length 3 feet / 2 feet / 1 foot. Read it with the Figure 38 drawing.
  • Seal all outer joints with the supplied high temperature self-adhesive aluminium tape, wrapped fully around; the inner pipe isn't sealed. Venting components named on p. 26: Simpson DuraVent, Secure Vent, Selkirk Direct-Temp and ICC ExcelDirect part numbers.
  • Terminal clearances: table on p. 25 (Canada / US), e.g. 12 inches above grade, veranda, porch, deck or balcony; mechanical air supply inlet 6 feet (1.8 m) min. in Canada, 3 feet min. above if within 10ft horizontally in the US. Terminal casing to combustibles: 0 in.
Note: the manual gives two vent-pipe clearances to combustibles: 1 3/4" (45 mm) from any part of the venting pipe on p. 5, in the p. 22 caution and on the rating label (1.75 in., p. 45), but 1.5 in. (38 mm) for vertical and horizontal vent pipe in the power vent installation clearances (p. 22) and a minimum 1½" clearance in Figure 37 (p. 23).
Propane conversion (if LP)

Kit TCWS.54DSTLPKIT, fitted by a qualified service agency with the gas and the breaker off: LC orifices, air shutters 3/16" open, pilot band to propane, then the SIT valve conversion with a new stepper. Fix the conversion label and confirm manifold pressure.

1. Remove any glass media, logs or rock set and the edge panels; remove the burner tray (screws to the burners and side panels, plus two at each end into the side panels).
  2. Lift the burners off the orifices (pilot assembly too if needed). With a 1/2" wrench, swap the natural gas orifices for the kit's propane orifices, with a little pipe joint compound on the threads.
  3. Loosen the primary air shutter screw on each burner, open the shutter to a 3/16" gap and re-tighten.
  4. Loosen the pilot head with a 7/16" wrench and slide the pilot adjustment band until the hole shows (propane position).
  5. Valve access: remove the burner media, edge panels, burner tray, left hand burner and left hand side panel, release the pilot assembly from the center leg, then remove the left hand secondary floor panel and the large cover panel.
  6. Disconnect the stepper's wires, remove its two screws (discard them and use the two new ones in the kit) and finish per the SIT propane gas conversion kit instructions.
  7. Fill out the conversion label (5052.52001-B) and fix it inside the control box, away from firebox heat. Reinstall the control box shield and the access panel.
Check gas pressures

With the fireplace lit on its highest setting, check supply (NG 5.0"–13.9" WC, LP 12.5"–13.9" WC) and manifold pressure (NG 1.6"–3.5" WC, LP 6.4"–10" WC). Turn the gas off before pulling a test-port plug (3/16" hex key) and refit it with thread sealant.
Panels, burner, trim & flame check

Fit the side panels, the burner and the porcelain edge strips (short flange toward the burners), then the Finishing Touch trim kit and the magnetic safety barrier screen. Let it run 30 minutes, then set the air shutter for a just orange, lazy, soot-free flame.

1. Firebox panels: remove the side panel securing tabs in the upper firebox, set each side panel in bottom first and tip it up, then refit the tabs. Install the burner, then place the porcelain edge strips with their short flange facing the burners and media.
  2. Burners: the replacement parts lists cover a Tranquility burner kit (TCWS.54NGST04D, pebble assembly and sand) and a Diamond burner (TCWS.54NGST03D, glass media: 5lb bags, 2 required). Follow the instructions supplied with the burner kit.
  3. Finishing Touch trim kit (TCRP.54WSTRIMKIT): side pieces first (2 small button magnets each), then the top piece over them (2 larger magnets); the meshed bottom piece rests on the floor in the gap between the frame and the glass door. Badge on the lower right corner of the safety screen.
  4. Attach the magnetic safety barrier screen to the outer-most door frame. The appliance is for use only with the glass and screen barrier certified with it.

Flame check

The air shutter is closed at the factory for natural gas. Judge the flame after 30 minutes, at operating temperature (Figure 67, p. 38). Open primary air if carbon builds up on the door glass and firebox or the flames are long, dark and stringy; opening it also lessens flame height. The flame should be just orange and "lazy", never set to soot internal parts or the glass.

panels.title: Soot or poor flame
items: Carbon on the door glass and firebox, or long, dark, stringy flames → open the primary air shutter
Flame too tall → opening the shutter also lessens flame height
Excessive soot on the pebble and burner assemblies → qualified service person inspects and adjusts for proper combustion
Flame judged too soon → run 30 minutes and evaluate at operating temperature

panels.title: Won't light or won't respond
items: Slow to ignite → it may take up to 30 seconds each time ON is selected; the first time, allow for air to escape from the lines
Burner doesn't light → switch OFF, wait at least 5 minutes, smell for gas. If you still smell gas, stop. If not, retry
Won't light or stay lit after several tries → switch OFF, turn off all electric power, call a service technician or gas supplier
Remote has no effect → the wall switch toggle must be kept on REMOTE
A nearby fireplace responds instead → repeat the wall switch-to-fireplace link to move to another of three channels
Remote batteries low or depleted → turn the fireplace off with the wall switch ON/OFF switch

light.title: Turning the fireplace on and off
light.html:
An igniter lights the pilot automatically, so never try to light it by hand. Each time you switch it on, it can take up to 30 seconds to ignite.

Every day

Press ON/OFF on the remote. A single beep from the fireplace confirms the command. Press it again to turn the fire off. The selector on the wall switch must be on REMOTE for the remote to work.

Lighting steps (from the lighting label)

  1. Read the safety information on the label. Smell all around the fireplace for gas, next to the floor too.
  2. Push the On/Off switch on the wall to turn the fireplace on. If the burner lights, set the flame you want with the remote.
  3. If it doesn't light, push the switch to off. Wait at least 5 minutes for any gas in the combustion chamber to clear. Still smell gas? Stop and follow the gas-smell steps under Safety. No smell? Try step 2 again.
The very first time, allow time for air to escape from the gas lines.
Won't light or stay lit after several tries? Push the On/Off switch to off, turn off all electric power to the fireplace and call your service technician or gas supplier.

To turn it off, push the On/Off switch to off. For service or a long shutdown, also turn off all electric power to it.

remote.title: Using the remote
remote.html:
The Proflame 2 remote has a blue back-lit screen and four controls: ON/OFF, THERMOSTAT, MODE and the up/down arrows. It takes 3 AAA batteries. Keep the wall switch selector on REMOTE. A single beep from the fireplace confirms your commands.

Flame height

There are six flame levels. With the flame at maximum, each press of the down arrow lowers it one step, down to off. The up arrow raises it. If the fireplace is on but the flame is off, the up arrow brings the flame back on high.

Light

Press MODE until the light bulb icon shows, then use the arrows to pick one of six levels.

Key lock

Press MODE and the up arrow together to lock the keys against unsupervised use. A lock icon appears. Press them together again to unlock.

Pilot mode

With the system off, press MODE to reach the CPI icon. The up arrow selects continuous pilot ignition (CPI); the down arrow returns to intermittent pilot ignition (IPI).

The thermostat function is off by default. The manual says it isn't permissible in the USA (it is in Canada).

sounds.title: First fire: smells, sounds and beeps
sounds.html:
A slight odor at first

The first time it's lit, the fireplace gives off a slight odor for a couple of hours while paints, sealants and lubricants from manufacturing cure. It's temporary. Open doors and windows to air out the room; the odor can bother some people.

Ticks and creaks

It's normal for a steel fireplace to make some expansion and contraction noises as it starts up or cools down, much like a furnace heat exchanger or an oven.

A pause before it lights

It can take up to 30 seconds to ignite each time you switch it on. The igniter sparks, and after a short delay the pilot lights, followed by the main burner.

A beep

A single beep from the fireplace means it received a command from the remote.

A gas smell is different. Don't light anything, touch electrical switches or use a phone in your building. Call your gas supplier from a neighbour's phone. See Safety.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Clean the viewing glass as needed with fireplace glass cleaner, and only when it's cool. Hot glass will cause burns.

  • Turn off the gas and electrical power and give the fireplace plenty of time to cool before servicing it.
  • Don't use abrasive cleaners on the glass or any other part of the fireplace.
  • Clean the outside finish with mild soap and water.

Cracked or broken glass

Never run the fireplace with the glass removed, cracked or broken, and don't strike or knock the glass. Replacement should be done by a licensed or qualified service person, with ceramic glass only. Replacement glass comes from your nearest Town & Country dealer.

Keep the safety barrier screen in place. It's there to reduce the risk of burns from the hot glass.

app.title: Wall switch, pairing and the TC Fire app
app.html:
The wall switch is the fireplace's wall-mounted receiver, and the remote links to it. Pair things in this order; the first two steps are needed even if you only plan to use the app.

  1. Wall switch to fireplace: set the wall switch selector to Remote. With a straightened paper clip, press and hold the Program button for up to 10 seconds, until the wall switch beeps 5 times, then let go. The fireplace beeps 3 times, then 3 more: they're linked.
  2. Remote to wall switch: press and release the Program button once (3 beeps). Within 60 seconds, press and release ON/OFF on the remote. Three beeps from the wall switch mean they're paired.
If a nearby fireplace turns on instead of yours, repeat step 1. It switches to another of three available channels.

TC Fire app (optional)

Get the free TC Fire app from the Apple App Store or Google Play for a Bluetooth phone. Open Add/Edit Fireplace, press Add, enter the PIN from the sticker on the wall switch and a name for the fireplace, then press Save. The app turns the flame and the light on and off and sets their levels. You'll only see your fireplace when your phone is within Bluetooth range and no one else is controlling it.

power.title: Power and batteries
power.html:
The fireplace runs on house electricity, and its venting uses a powered vent.

  • Wall switch: it has a battery holder, but on this fireplace the holder must stay empty. The installation manual says those batteries would be a backup for power outages, and this fireplace must not operate on battery backup.
  • Remote: 3 AAA batteries. A battery icon shows on its screen before they run out and goes away once you replace them. How long they last depends on battery quality and how often the fireplace lights.
  • Remote dead or not working? Turn the fireplace off with the On/Off switch on the wall switch.

Backup batteries

The Owner's Manual's general Proflame 2 text also describes a battery pack that can back up the control module, used only when line power is interrupted or lost and only if the fireplace doesn't use a combustion fan, and a double-beep from the module when those batteries are low (pp. 7, 10). That backup isn't for this fireplace: it is power vented, the wall switch must not have batteries and the fireplace must not operate with a battery back up (Installation Manual pp. 18–19), and the battery holder must remain empty (Owner's Manual p. 7). The lighting label also says to remove backup batteries if service is to be performed or for an extended shutdown (Owner's Manual p. 4); with the holder empty, there are none to remove.

safety.title: Safety and gas smell
safety.html:
If you smell gas

  • Don't try to light any appliance.
  • Don't touch any electrical switch, and don't use any phone in your building.
  • Call your gas supplier right away from a neighbour's phone and follow their instructions. If you can't reach them, call the fire department.

Before lighting, smell all around the fireplace, next to the floor too: some gas is heavier than air and settles there.

Around the fireplace

  • Hot glass will cause burns. Don't touch it until it has cooled, and never let children touch it. Keep the safety barrier screen installed.
  • Supervise young children in the room. A safety gate can keep toddlers and other at-risk people away from hot surfaces.
  • Keep clothing, furniture, drapes and anything flammable away. Never store or use gasoline or other flammable vapors and liquids nearby.
  • Put back any panel or door removed for service before using the fireplace.
  • Use only your hand to push in or turn the gas control knob, and never use tools. If the knob won't push in or turn by hand, don't try to repair it. Call a qualified service technician. Force or attempted repair may result in a fire or explosion.
  • Don't use the fireplace if any part has been under water. Call a qualified service technician right away to inspect it and to replace any part of the control system and any gas control that has been under water.
This is a decorative fireplace. The manual says it isn't intended to be used as a heating appliance.

service.title: Yearly service
service.html:
Have the fireplace inspected before use and at least once a year by a qualified service person, venting included. Lint from carpets, bedding and the like can mean cleaning more often. The control compartments, burners and air passageways must be kept clean.

What the yearly inspection covers

  • Removing the glass panel and any pebble assemblies and checking them and the burner for soot. Heavy soot means the fireplace needs inspecting and adjusting for proper combustion. Burners are cleaned with a brush or vacuum, with care at the burner ports.
  • Checking the pilot flame size and operation, and cleaning soot and dust off the pilot.
  • Making sure the vent pipe and vent terminal are open and free of blockage or debris.
  • Checking the glass gasket and replacing it if needed. A good glass seal matters.
  • Checking and replacing batteries as needed.

The flame should be just orange and "lazy", never set so it leaves soot on the inside parts or the glass.

Before any servicing, turn off the gas and electrical power and let the fireplace cool. Don't try to repair it yourself; contact your dealer.

bulb.title: Replacing the light bulb
bulb.html:
The light sits at the top of the firebox. As with any servicing, turn off the gas and electrical power and let the fireplace cool first.

Take out the old bulb

  1. Remove the screw holding the light cover to the upper heat shield at the top of the firebox, then pull the light assembly down slightly.
  2. Slip a small flat screwdriver between the glass lens and the light box, and twist carefully to pop the lens open.
  3. Pull the old bulb away from the plug end, wiggling it gently.

Put in the new bulb

  1. Hold it with a paper towel or cloth, not your fingers: skin oils can make it fail early. If you touch it by accident, clean it with alcohol before use.
  2. Push it into the plug end, wiggling it gently.
  3. Push the glass lens up to close it.
  4. Seat the plug end of the light assembly in the light box and fasten it with the screw you removed.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Town & Country's limited lifetime warranty for gas products covers the original registered purchaser.

Limited lifetime, parts onlyGlass (thermal breakage only), combustion chamber, burner tube assembly, porcelain finishes
2 years, parts and laborAny part found defective, from the original date of purchase

Conditions

  • A qualified technician installs it to local and national requirements and to the appliance manual, with sediment traps within 6 feet of the gas control valve, and makes sure it fires as per the rating plate.
  • Porcelain is warranted for gloss retention. Some colors darken when hot and return to their shade when cool, and as a man-made finish it can have minor imperfections.
  • Town & Country decides whether a defective part is repaired, replaced or refunded.

Not covered

  • Misuse, abuse, improper installation, accident or lack of maintenance.
  • Mantels, surrounds or finishing material around the fireplace.
  • Installation, operating or environmental conditions beyond Town & Country's control.
This is a summary; the full terms, including limits on damages, are in the manual. The manual also says any installation or operating deviation from its instructions voids the warranty.

Listed to ANSI Z21.50-2016 / CSA 2.22-2016 (vented gas fireplaces) and CAN/CGA 2.17-M91 (high altitudes). The label is on a plate in a slot between the left hand side lintel and the left hand side door frame, attached to the side casing with a cable. Making sure the appliance fires as per the rating plate is the installer's responsibility (warranty condition).

The minimums are for the purpose of input adjustment. Verify pressures with the fireplace lit and on the highest setting. Turn off the gas before removing the plug from the supply or manifold pressure test port, thread in the extension test fitting and attach the gauge; afterwards shut off the gas, remove the fitting and refit the plug with thread sealant.

Piping tests: disconnect the appliance and its shut-off valve above 1/2 psig (3.5 kPa); close its manual shut-off valve for tests at or below 1/2 psig.

specManifold.html:

From the gas pressure check table (p. 34); the rating label lists the maximums as 3.5 in/wc (0.87 kPa) for natural gas and 10.0 in/wc (2.49 kPa) for LP. Check with the fireplace lit and on its highest setting. After a propane conversion, confirm proper manifold pressure.

specVent.title: Power venting
specVent.html:
This fireplace must be power vented. Wall termination only with the TCVT.PV1.25 or TCVT.PV7.110 power vent kit; roof termination with TCVT.PVCV. Follow the instructions supplied with the kit.

Max total vent length110 ft plus six 90-degree elbows (or a combination of other elbows equaling 90-degrees)
Max vertical rise66 ft
Min total vent length3 ft plus one 90-degree elbow
Below the unitup to 3 ft, to the center of the vent pipe
Vent supportsa minimum of 1 every 4'
TCVT.PV1.25 speed0 - 6': LOW · 7'- 25': HIGH
TCVT.PV7.110 speed7'- 25': LOW · 26'-110': HIGH

Keep the vent short with as few elbows as possible for the best performance and flame appearance. Join components tightly, secure them with sheet metal screws and seal every outer joint with the supplied high temperature self-adhesive tape. Venting components named on p. 26: Simpson DuraVent, Secure Vent, Selkirk Direct-Temp and ICC ExcelDirect. The rating label also lists TCVT.PVVT among the power vent kits; the venting section doesn't mention it.

Note: the manual gives two vent-pipe clearances to combustibles: 1 3/4" (45 mm) from any part of the venting pipe on p. 5, in the p. 22 caution and on the rating label (1.75 in., p. 45), but 1.5 in. (38 mm) for vertical and horizontal vent pipe in the power vent installation clearances (p. 22) and a minimum 1½" clearance in Figure 37 (p. 23).

The assembled framing kit acts as the top and side standoffs. Mantel clearance and depth follow the stepped mantel chart, which the manual gives only as a drawing (Figure 2, p. 5: mantel clearances A–C and mantel depths D–F). Keep the fireplace out of traffic and away from furniture and draperies. On carpet, tile or other combustible flooring other than wood, set it on a metal or wood panel the full width and depth of the appliance.

Note: the manual gives two vent-pipe clearances to combustibles: 1 3/4" (45 mm) from any part of the venting pipe on p. 5, in the p. 22 caution and on the rating label (1.75 in., p. 45), but 1.5 in. (38 mm) for vertical and horizontal vent pipe in the power vent installation clearances (p. 22) and a minimum 1½" clearance in Figure 37 (p. 23).

specFrame.title: Framing and finishing
specFrame.html:
Steel stud framing kitSupplied; must be used unless totally enclosed in non-combustible material
Non-combustible backer board12" above and 5 9/16" to the side of the framing edge bars
Calcium silicate board1/2" thick

Combustible hearth6" min. below the bottom of the glass door
Door frame openingobjects higher than 11 9/16" interfere

The lintel is fixed, so the fireplace itself is positioned to set the front. The steel stud zone is non-combustible: no combustible material, electrical wiring, insulation, plastic vapor barrier or gas plumbing inside it. The sides and top can be framed up to the steel studs with conventional lumber. Minimum combustible framing dimensions are a drawing only (Figure 13, p. 9). Finishing material must never stop the door or the screen from opening.

Note: the manual gives two recess depths. It says the unit may be recessed up to 6" with noncombustible masonry type material (p. 5) and that masonry type non-combustible material can go up to 6 inches forward of the appliance (p. 8), but gives a 4 1/2 inch recess on p. 15 and a 4 1/2 maximum facing depth in Figure 12 (p. 9).

specElec.html:

The gas and electrical controls sit below the firebox floor on the left hand side. Set the NV / PV switch on the IFC board to PV (pushed away from you); this model must be pre-set to PV. No batteries in the wall switch: its battery holder must remain empty. Electrical work by a qualified electrician to CSA C22.1 / ANSI/NFPA 70 and local codes; never use a rheostat to alter the supply voltage. The wiring diagram (p. 44) is a drawing only.

Note: p. 17 rates the power vent kit at 115 volts, 60Hz, 1.8A; the rating label (p. 45) lists a blower electrical rating of 115v, 60hz, 1.1 A. The manual mentions no blower anywhere else, so these may or may not be the same part.

The appliance is only for the gas on its rating plate unless a certified kit is used. Shut off the gas supply and the electrical power at the breaker first. A qualified service agency installs the kit with the factory supplied components and checks the converted appliance's operation; afterwards confirm proper manifold pressure. Reinstall the control box shield and the access panel, or the control system will overheat and fail early.

Wait at least 5 minutes; if you still smell gas, stop. If not, retry; after several tries, call service

conflicts.issue: Recess depth (also shown in step3): p. 5 (Figure 3 note) says the unit may be recessed up to 6" with noncombustible masonry type material and p. 8 says masonry type non-combustible material can be installed up to 6 inches forward of the appliance; p. 15 says the fireplace can be installed with a 4 1/2 inch recess and Figure 12 (p. 9) marks a 4 1/2 maximum facing depth.

Vent pipe clearance to combustibles (also shown in specVent and step6): 1 3/4" (45 mm) in the minimum clearances (p. 5), in the venting caution ('closer than 1 3/4 inches from any part of the venting pipe', p. 22) and on the rating label (1.75 in., p. 45); but the TCVT.PV power vent installation clearances give 1.5 in. (38 mm) for vertical and horizontal vent pipe (p. 22) and Figure 37 says 'minimum 1½" clearance to combustable surfaces from vent pipe' (p. 23).

Battery backup: the Installation Manual says not to install batteries in the wall switch, the battery holder must remain empty, and 'This fireplace must not operate with a battery back up' (pp. 18-19); the Owner's Manual repeats that the holder must remain empty (p. 7). But the Owner's Manual lighting label says to 'remove backup batteries if service is to be performed or for extended shutdown' (p. 4), its IFC description gives a battery pack for back up, used only when line power is lost and if the fireplace does not use a combustion fan (p. 7), and it describes a double-beep for low IFC batteries (p. 10).
conflicts.reason: On a second read the battery statements fit together. The Owner's Manual's battery-pack and low-IFC-battery text (pp. 7, 10) is general Proflame 2 description that itself limits battery back-up to fireplaces that don't use a combustion fan; for this power-vented fireplace the Installation Manual says the wall switch must not have batteries and it must not operate with a battery back up (pp. 18-19), and the Owner's Manual says on the same p. 7 that the battery holder must remain empty. The lighting label's step to remove backup batteries for service or extended shutdown (Owner's p. 4) has nothing to act on when the holder is empty. The power drawer now explains this in plain text instead of a box.

conflicts.issue: Fan electrical rating: p. 17 rates the power vent kit at 115 volts, 60Hz, 1.8A; the rating label lists 'Blower electrical rating: 115v, 60hz, 1.1 A' (p. 45). The manual names no blower anywhere else, so it is unclear whether these describe the same part.

review.notes: Text layer: Installation Manual p. 44 (wiring diagram) carries only its heading and pp. 46-47 only footers; Owner's Manual pp. 21-23 only footers. Figure-only content the guide points to instead of transcribing: fireplace dimensions (Figure 1, p. 5: unlabeled numbers); the stepped mantel chart (Figure 2, p. 5: mantel clearances A 9", B 6", C 3" and mantel depths D 12", E 6 3/4", F 1 1/2", whose pairing and reference point are only in the drawing; the guide uses only the rating label's text values, mantel to appliance 9 in. and maximum mantel extension 12 in., p. 45); framing kit and minimum combustible framing dimensions (Figures 9 and 13, pp. 8-9); recess details (Figures 12 and 14); the vent terminal drawing (Figure 39; the p. 25 table is text and two rows are quoted); the wiring diagram (p. 44); the flame pattern (Figure 67, p. 38). The minimum vent length chart (p. 24) is transcribed with its A-C column headings; where A-C are measured is only in Figure 38. Input rates appear only on the rating label (p. 45). No vent pipe diameter is stated in the text (p. 26 lists components by part number only), so none is given. Cross-reference drift: the Installation Manual's table of contents runs one page behind the physical pages (e.g. Gas Pressure Check Procedure listed at 33, actually p. 34; Propane Conversion listed at 27, actually p. 28, which the p. 2 note gets right); p. 8 points to framing kit instructions on 'pages 10 - 12' (actually pp. 11-13). The Owner's Manual (p. 17) refers to a 'Window Frame Removal' section it doesn't contain; the procedure is 'Door Frame Removal' in the Installation Manual (p. 6). Burner Flame Adjustment (p. 38) cites 'Figure 66' for the flame pattern (the flame figure is 67; Figure 66 is the safety barrier screen) and its sentence 'For LP .' is cut off, so no propane flame guidance is taken from that page; the 3/16" propane shutter gap comes from the conversion procedure (p. 29). Model designations vary: TCWS54DST, Series D, Version 2 (covers); TCWS54DST2 (Installation footers) and TCWS54DST_Ver2 (Owner footers); TCWS54ST, Series D (rating label); TCWS54STD2, TCWS54D2 and TCWS54.DST in the text. The power vent kit is written TCVT. PV1.25 (p. 22), TCVT.PV1.25 (p. 23) and TCVT.PVI.25 (rating label); the label also lists TCVT.PVVT, which the venting section doesn't mention (noted in the specVent drawer), and calls the power vent kits 'optional components' although p. 22 says the fireplace must be power vented. Facing: p. 8 says 3/4" facing finishes flush with the front of the unit and p. 15 says facing up to 1 7/8" can be accommodated when installing flush (the framing kit has 1 7/8" of adjustment, p. 13); both are stated, not treated as a conflict. The Owner's Manual's generic Proflame 2 text mentions a comfort fan with six speeds, an auxiliary outlet, a Smart thermostat and an IFC battery pack; no comfort fan is described for this model, so the guide has no fan tile, and the thermostat is given as disabled by default and not permissible in the USA. The lighting label's item C (gas control knob) is generic and the lighting steps never use a knob; the guide still gives it in the Safety drawer, with its fire-or-explosion consequence. The Attention box on Owner's Manual p. 6 says to turn off the main gas supply before removing or reinserting 'the batteries' without saying which batteries; not used. The faults panels are built from the manual's fault descriptions (Burner Flame Adjustment p. 38, annual inspection p. 39, lighting label p. 4, pairing and manual-bypass notes on Owner's pp. 8 and 11, Installation p. 19); the manual has no troubleshooting chart and no code table. Orifices are identified only as NC (natural gas) and LC (propane), x2 each on the label; no drill size is given. Manifold minimums come only from the p. 34 table (the label shows maximums). Catalog view_area (748 sq in) and the features list aren't checked against the manual text; efficiency 30.7% (P.4.1-15) and the catalog clearances note match the manual. check_numbers: every number in the guide was found in the manual text.
